title: Career roadmap · Innovation Head
summary: Build from interdisciplinary research into technology translation, venture creation, R&D portfolio management and organisation-wide innovation leadership.

facts.Current degree: D.Sc / D.Litt / DBA / Post-Doctoral & Industry-Sponsored Doctorates
facts.Course: Interdisciplinary Ph.D. (Data Science, Sustainability, Public Health, Cognitive Science, Bioengineering, Energy)
facts.Timeline assumption: This roadmap assumes the student already has a doctorate-level research background and is moving toward innovation leadership. Because the course combines very different fields, the strongest route is to choose one technical or societal domain while developing a common innovation stack: research translation, IP, product development, partnerships, funding, venture strategy and portfolio management.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Innovation fellow, technology-transfer researcher, R&D programme manager, venture/innovation associate or research-innovation lead.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Become a specialist in one innovation domain such as AI/data, climate/energy, healthtech, bioengineering or deep-tech commercialisation.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Lead multi-project innovation portfolios, corporate/university partnerships, technology-transfer programmes and new ventures.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Become an enterprise innovation leader connecting research, capital, technology, markets, regulation and organisational transformation.

items: Chief Innovation Officer / Enterprise Innovation Leader
blocks.label: Career progression
Typical years
blocks.text:
2026–2030 → research translation and innovation-programme experience
2030–2035 → innovation/R&D management
2035–2040 → innovation portfolio leadership
2040–2046 → enterprise-level innovation leadership
Ph.D./research routes

The senior Innovation Head should be able to manage an innovation portfolio rather than a single project. That means balancing long-horizon research with near-term product opportunities, allocating capital across uncertain projects, building external partnerships, managing IP and regulatory risk, and creating pathways from laboratory results to adoption. The strongest profile will combine scientific credibility with business judgement and organisational leadership.
